caption_review: Neither caption only repeats a title: the landing fragment's caption names the partition and gives the day's five totals, and the landed record's caption explains that both series come from the same partition, so each adds interpretation rather than echoing the figure's name.

figures.caption: Hours waited by stage per delivered run, the baseline week against the measured day on one axis. The baseline's larger no-stage-receipt share is the runs that stayed delivered for days before the record was taken. Totals for the day are 174 h, 214 h, 43 h, 2.6 h and 1.9 h in the order shown.

rubric_items.contrast: pass - measured on the rendered PNG: tick and axis labels #0b0b0b (19.68:1 on white), stage labels #52514e (7.94:1), grey series value labels #5a5a5a (6.90:1), blue series value labels #1f77b4 (4.82:1, above the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold and well above the 3:1 large-text threshold); every text run clears its white or bar background.
rubric_items.data_ink: pass - the ink is five pairs of solid bars, four tick labels, five stage labels, ten value labels, two axis labels and one legend; no value is carried by decoration alone and no ink is spent on material the data do not use.
rubric_items.decoration: pass - no gradient, no background fill, no gridlines or shading, top and right spines absent, legend unframed; bars are flat colour, so nothing decorative competes with the data.
rubric_items.label_collision: pass - the rendered ink bounding box is x 16..1379, y 20..698 inside a 1400x720 canvas, so nothing is clipped on any edge; no two text runs overlap, and no value label sits over a plotted bar (each is placed beyond its bar end, and the two labels of a pair sit on separate rows, e.g. 0.38 above 0.28).
rubric_items.legibility: pass - five stage labels read left of grouped horizontal bars and each bar carries its numeric value at its end (1.54/4.65, 1.89/0.36, 0.38/0.28, 0.02/0.03, 0.02/0.00); a reader gets every value at a glance without consulting the caption.
rubric_items.table_form: pass - the image is a two-series comparison across five ordered stages, which reads better as grouped bars than as a table; no information in it is naturally tabular only.
